Containers are rooms in one house: they all stand on the host computer's one kernel, the core of its operating system. Virtual machines are separate houses: each one boots its own operating system, kernel included. Virtual machines run separate kernels, and containers share one. Here is why that shared foundation matters, starting with the ark.
sov100-rooms-shalt-thou-make-in-the-ark.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Do your apps share a room or a house? In a container, your app is a room on a shared foundation: quick to start, light to carry, and only as safe as the one kernel under every room. In a virtual machine, it is a house on its own foundation: heavier, but a break-in has a second wall to climb. So choose by what needs keeping apart, give a stranger's code its own house, lock every room down to the powers it needs, and never trust any wall as if it were the Keeper.
